reports.title: Analog Devices Reports Record Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2026 Financial Results

guidance.heading: Outlook for the First Quarter of Fiscal Year 2027
section: For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, we are forecasting revenue of $4.4 billion, +/- $150 million. At the midpoint of this revenue outlook, we expect reported operating margin of approximately 40.3%, +/- 150 bps, and adjusted operating margin of approximately 50.5%, +/- 100 bps. We are planning for reported EPS to be $3.02, +/- $0.20, and adjusted EPS to be $3.82, +/- $0.20.

The adjusted results and adjusted anticipated results above are financial measures presented on a non-GAAP basis. Reconciliations of these non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable GAAP financial measures are provided in the financial tables included in this release. See also the “Non-GAAP Financial Information” section for additional information.

desk.headline: Revenue up 42% to $4.37bn and adjusted EPS of $4.06, both above estimates; Q1 outlook of $4.4bn, roughly flat on Q4
results: Q4 revenue rose 42% to a record $4.37bn, above the $4.32bn estimate; adjusted EPS of $4.06 beat the $3.88 estimate.
Every end market grew: communications +81%, industrial +55%, automotive +21% and consumer +7%.
Margins widened sharply: adjusted gross margin 74.5% (from 69.8%) and adjusted operating margin 52.3% (from 43.5%).
Full year: revenue $15.2bn (+38%), adjusted EPS $13.05 (+68%) and free cash flow $5.5bn, or 36% of revenue.
ADI returned $5.4bn in FY26 through dividends and buybacks, and declared a quarterly dividend of $1.10.

guidance.summary: For Q1 FY27 ADI expects revenue of about $4.4bn (plus or minus $150m) and adjusted EPS of about $3.82, slightly below Q4's $4.06. It gives one quarter of guidance only.

points: CEO Vincent Roche said AI infrastructure is driving data centre and chip-testing sales, but over two-thirds of FY26 growth came from other markets.
Data centre sales were 13% of revenue and more than doubled again; the CFO expects strong growth there in FY27.
The Q1 outlook implies slight growth on Q4, better than the usual seasonal dip; consumer is seen falling 10–15% and auto slightly lower.
Orders exceeded shipments in almost every market, with no sign of customers over-stocking.
Capital spending will rise to $1.6–1.9bn in FY27 from about $700m to add factory capacity, as supply stays tight.
call.source: Call coverage: MarketBeat via Yahoo Finance, 24 Nov 2026

watch: Whether demand holds up after the sharp FY26 rebound, given the roughly flat Q1 outlook.
Gross margin, which management expects to ease to about 74% in Q1.
Progress on the much bigger FY27 capacity spending and tight supply.
